findings.class: lane-owned defect, fixed this run with a mutation test
findings.title: A configure that does not complete discarded every dependency header it had already fetched, so ten compilable examples were recorded NOT_VERIFIED and a required contract row lost its evidence.
findings.detail: build_product returned ('configure failed', []) the moment the configure step exited non-zero, throwing away fetched_includes(build) - the include directories that same step had already written to disk. Aspose.Slides for C++'s public shape_collection.h opens with `#include <pugixml.hpp>`, so without pugixml's include directory every one of its ten examples stops at that line with a fatal error in a header rather than a diagnostic of its own, and the verifier honestly records NOT_VERIFIED / BLOCKED_TOOLCHAIN for all ten. Measured on this repository: the run's own workspace `runs/verify/dd476f154c80/cmake-build/_deps` held `pugixml-build`, `pugixml-src` and `pugixml-subbuild` and nothing else - the configure had fetched pugixml and been cut off before miniz and GoogleTest - while `_deps/pugixml-src/src/pugixml.hpp`, exactly the directory fetched_includes returns, was on disk the whole time. The cost was not ten receipts but a contract row: preflight read `required rows without evidence: quick_start`, because quick_start's only evidence kind is `example` and no example was SUPPORTED.
findings.evidence: Before: `examples: 10 candidates; not_verified 10`, `3011 facts, 3000 supported, 11 unresolved`, `required rows without evidence: quick_start`. After the one-line fix, same revision, same machine: `examples: 10 candidates; executed 9, not_verified 1`, `3011 facts, 3010 supported, 1 unresolved`, `required rows without evidence: none`. The single remaining NOT_VERIFIED is example 10, whose only diagnostics are unbound identifiers (`pres`, `SaveFormat`) - the documented incomplete-fence class, not a failure. Mutation tests: test_a_configure_cut_off_still_hands_back_what_it_already_fetched and test_a_configure_that_genuinely_failed_says_so_and_keeps_its_fetches.

findings.class: lane-owned defect, fixed this run with a mutation test
findings.title: The configure ceiling was below the measured spread of the step it bounds, and a receipt called a step that was cut off 'failed'.
findings.detail: _TIMEOUT_CONFIGURE was 180 s. The configure step is the network-bound one - FetchContent downloads one archive per find_package that finds nothing, and Aspose.Slides for C++ fetches three (pugixml v1.14, miniz 3.0.2, GoogleTest v1.15.2) - so its duration tracks the link, not the machine. Measured 2026-09-16, three cold configures of the same revision on the same machine: CMake reported `Configuring done` at 57.8 s, 71.7 s and 141.7 s, a 2.4x spread, and the run that produced this transaction's first receipts exceeded 180 s. Raised to 300 s, which is `core.execution.MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` - the most one bounded execution may be given at all, so no larger value is available to a platform module. Separately, the phrase the receipt carries now distinguishes 'configure timed out' from 'configure failed': saying a step failed when it was cut off is not true, and both phrases differ from 'succeeded', so build_verified stays false either way and TB-01 is not loosened.
findings.evidence: `_TIMEOUT_CONFIGURE = 600.0` was refused by the boundary with `ValueError: example timeout must be within (0, 300] seconds`, which is how the cap was found; the constant is 300.0 and test_the_configure_ceiling_clears_the_measured_download_spread pins it to MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and above twice the measured maximum. That the boundary caps a network-bound step at the same ceiling as a compile-bound one is PROPOSAL LANE-B-R5-P2 below; with F1 fixed it no longer costs a repository its examples, which is why it is a proposal and not a blocker.

findings.class: PROPOSAL - shared code the lane may not edit
findings.title: A presentation finding is never asked whether its own quote lies in the section it names, so F09 condemns enterprise_relationship while quoting scope_limitations and blocks BC-10.
findings.detail: F09 is the only finding of nine that survived the fold stack. It sets section_id `enterprise_relationship`, cites `link_target:product.enterprise`, and says 'The candidate's Enterprise Relationship section is promotional and adds no product-specific substance, while the original README does not contain such a section', with repair 'Remove the Enterprise Relationship section entirely'. Three independent refutations, each mechanical. (1) There is no such section: docs/README_CONTRACT.md row 18 gives enterprise_relationship the heading `none (closing paragraph of Scope and Limitations)`, and the candidate's heading list contains no Enterprise Relationship heading - the slot's single content unit renders as the closing sentence of `## Scope and Limitations` at line 634, in exactly row 18's prescribed shape, opening `These limitations don't apply to [Aspose.Slides for Cpp - Enterprise Edition](https://products.aspose.com/slides/cpp/)`. (2) The finding's own quote is not from the slot it faults: 'There is no API for these. The member named is the one that does not exist, so a call to it is a' is rendered at line 605, under `## Scope and Limitations` at line 594, and `_carried_by_units` reports no content unit wrote it - it is renderer-emitted lead-in to the absence table. (3) The cited fact is what makes the paragraph mandatory: `link_target:product.enterprise` is SUPPORTED with evidence `HTTP 200; enterprise target; platform level; slug cpp`, which is precisely row 18's condition 'a verified aspose.com product target exists in policy'. Why every fold returns None, replayed through the production functions on this run's own artifacts: `_STRUCTURAL_SECTIONS` is {document, structure} and enterprise_relationship is neither; `_DETERMINISTIC_SECTIONS` is nine sections and enterprise_relationship is not among them; `_SECTION_HEADINGS` is built only from shell sections that HAVE a heading, so the one slot the contract gives heading `none` can never match `_quoted_heading`; `_quoted_chrome` is None; and `cited_fact_defect`, arrival item 63's own guard, folds a presentation finding only when the quote contains the literal value of a cited SUPPORTED fact - here that value is a URL the quote does not contain. The rule that would have caught it on its merits, renderer_owned_defect's 'the reviewer judging against the original README as the standard of support rather than against the facts' (lane D PROPOSAL P16), is gated behind `_quoted_verified_fact`, which is scoped to `public_symbol` alone and so cannot reach a finding citing a `link_target`. Proposed: before the criterion switch, refute a finding whose quote is rendered in a section other than the one its own section_id names - the finding's evidence and its target disagree, which no reading of the criterion repairs.
findings.evidence: Replayed mechanically: absence_defect, excluded_evidence_defect, rendered_defect and renderer_owned_defect each returned None on F09 with this run's real content_units.json and README.md; production agrees, since F09 was recorded blocking rather than advisory. The docstring of renderer_owned_defect already names this exact repository for the sibling class - 'Measured 2026-09-06: Aspose.Slides was held unsealed by a finding asking for a "Links" section the shell does not define' - which is a finding inventing a section, where F09 is a finding deleting one the shell renders headingless.

findings.class: PROPOSAL - shared code the lane may not edit
findings.file: src/repository_presenter/components/readme/repair/ (the route from a review finding to a targeted_repair packet)
findings.title: A finding whose repair instruction is 'remove this slot' is routed to a stage that can only rewrite a unit, so the repair can obey it only by emitting an empty unit, which the schema refuses.
findings.detail: This is the mechanical proof that F09 is not repairable content work rather than an opinion about it. repairs.json holds exactly one attempt, labelled F09, section_id enterprise_relationship, stage S6, outcome `unrepairable`, re_raised [F09], with reason `targeted_repair: output rejected twice; last rejection: revised_output.units[0].fact_ids: [] should be non-empty; revised_output.units[0].text: '' should be non-empty`. The repair understood the instruction and tried to carry it out; the only expression of 'remove this' available to a unit revision is an empty unit, and a unit must cite facts and carry text. Whether a slot is composed at all is the plan's decision at S5 and the shell's at render time, never a unit's, so a finding asking for a slot's removal is either a scope defect (it is here, see F3) or a finding against the plan - and in neither case can S6 act on it. Proposed: a finding whose repair names removal of a whole section or slot is routed to the stage that owns that decision, or refused as unactionable at the point of routing, rather than spending two live calls proving a schema forbids the only reply.
findings.evidence: runs/.../repairs.json, the single attempt above; the run's ledger shows S11 with 4 provider calls and 0 cache reuses - two attempts per round across two rounds, all four response_invalid on the same empty-unit rejection. `repair: 0 repaired, 1 unrepairable recorded advisory, 1 re-raised after repair; the equivalent failure stands; rounds 2`.

findings.class: PROPOSAL - shared code the lane may not edit; low priority, not blocking
findings.title: One ceiling bounds both a compile-bound step and a network-bound one, so a platform module cannot give a dependency download more headroom than a build.
findings.detail: MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 300 and execute() refuses any larger timeout_seconds outright. A C++ configure that fetches three dependencies over HTTPS is bounded by the link, and this machine measured a 2.4x spread (57.8 s / 71.7 s / 141.7 s) on one repository at one revision; a slow enough link still exceeds 300 s and nothing in a platform module can raise it. Recorded rather than pressed, because LANE-B-R5-F1 removes the consequence: a configure that runs out of time now keeps the headers it fetched, so the examples are still verified and only build_verified is honestly withheld. Proposed, if the owner wants it at all: a per-call ceiling that distinguishes a fetch from a compile, or a documented exemption for the configure step.
findings.evidence: `ValueError: example timeout must be within (0, 300] seconds`, raised by core/execution.py:142 when _TIMEOUT_CONFIGURE was set to 600.0; five previously-green tests in test_cpp_examples.py went red on it, which is how it was found.
